rites.name: Ilyeniomiel
rites.text: Ilyeniomiel is the concept of the Singing in Breroldock, the sounding through which the first roots of the world were drawn together. It is remembered as a low hum that settled into soil and stone during the Age of Sundering, when new land broke apart old bonds between peoples.

rites.name: Kelordock
rites.text: Kelordock is the Grounded counterpart realm of Breroldock, a sunken inversion of light where pale ash-lichen drinks heat from anything that enters. Its inhabitants, the Hollow Wardens, bind travelers to slow obsidian bells that toll only when a mind surrenders its name.

rites.name: Pelasten
rites.text: Pelasten is a creeping rot of hollowed-out ash and bruised light that clings to whatever it touches, slowly unmaking flesh and bone into something patient and hungry. In the Grounded realm of Breroldock it spreads through wells, relics, and the forgotten corners of old villages, leaving only husks that still walk.

rites.name: Kelaren
rites.text: Kelaren is a concept in Breroldock, the grove-lattice that the first sovereign used to bind the splintered shards of a broken world into one growing kingdom. Its roots remember the Fall, and its sap is said to hold the oath of the Pact in every ring of its bark.

rites.name: Thodon
rites.text: Thodon is a concept born in Breroldock's Walled Age, when centuries of holding walls, rival orders and first crossings shaped daily life. It is the notion of a sealed rite that binds a temple's flame to a single gate, letting its keepers hold a crossing against siege. Its power is limited to the reach of stone and fire.

rites.name: Brornelden
rites.text: Brornelden is a hand-cranked brass cannon from the Breroldock foundries, built to loose a concussive pulse that flings clustered crowds of the undead backward across the dirt. Its ceiling sits at roughly ten billion joules, making it a battlefield-scale tool rather than a city-wrecker. Engineers still argue over whether its recoil or its blast does more damage.

rites.name: Pelurath
rites.text: Pelurath is a concept of a ritual sigil-blade forged in the Grounded realm during the sixth era, said to bind the wielder's flesh to a hunched, many-jawed beast-form for a short span. While transformed, the bearer's strikes gain brutal weight, and each blow drinks in the warmth of nearby stone.

rites.name: Tarnudath
rites.text: Tarnudath is a bitter, sparkling tonic brewed in the cisterns of Breroldock's lower wards, said to thicken the blood and harden the skin of whoever drinks it. Its effect fades within a single day, leaving the drinker briefly more durable than any ordinary body should be.

rites.name: Pelalde
rites.text: Pelalde is a quiet, grounded reflex-art practiced by the lamp-keepers of Breroldock's flooded lowlands, who train their hands until loading and fastening feel almost instantaneous. Its adepts can slap a new magazine into place or drop a plank across a shutter in the span of a held breath. The art is prized for its discipline rather than its force, and the keepers never claim it changes anything beyond the hand.

rites.name: Pelerneld
rites.text: Pelerneld is a tincture brewed by the marsh-wardens of Breroldock from reed-pollen and cold spring water, prized for knitting flesh faster than any salve. Its makers claim a drinker may be drawn back from death a small number of times before the tincture's virtue is spent.

rites.name: Moruroneld
rites.text: Moruroneld is a bitter tonic brewed in the marsh-kilns of Breroldock, said to quicken the pulse of whoever swallows it. Later distillers refined it into a sharper draught that occasionally doubles the flash of a single shot.

rites.name: Thanordath
rites.text: Thanordath is a grounded combat discipline taught in the cliff-monasteries of Breroldock, where practitioners learn to turn their own falls into weapons. Its adepts are immune to the blasts and drops they bring upon themselves, and a practiced dive becomes a detonation that clears the ground beneath them, even scorching away lava and stone hazards.

rites.name: Joruldarnon
rites.text: Joruldarnon is a pale amber tonic brewed by the wayfinder couriers of Breroldock's high plateaus, prized for letting a runner keep a fast stride for hours without the burning weariness that ordinarily ends a sprint. It sharpens the drinker's pace and quiets the ache in muscle and lung alike, though its makers warn that the body pays later with a deep, dragging exhaustion.

rites.name: Morusten
rites.text: Morusten is a neural-tuning draught brewed in the lantern-towns of Breroldock, prized by wardens who hunt the hollow-eyed dead. Once it takes hold, the drinker's gaze settles on the faint seam where a skull is weakest whenever they sight along a barrel. Its effect is purely attentional and small in scale, bounded by the ordinary limits of a human body.

rites.name: Halardeld
rites.text: Halardeld is the quiet keepsake a Breroldock wanderer leaves behind when their thread of life frays, a small grey stone that hums faintly until its owner returns. Those who reclaim it within the hour find every hard-won gift of their former self settling back into their bones as though nothing had been lost. Its power is strictly personal and stays inert in any other hand.

rites.name: Pelurnock
rites.text: Pelurnock is a sticky, acid-threaded resin that gathers at the edge of every blow and hangs in the air like a fresh spider's snare. Survivors who fall in a fight release a shimmering veil that briefly absorbs incoming harm while the resin clings to whatever lurches close.

rites.name: Draldeste
rites.text: Draldeste is a sparking tonic brewed by wandering apothecaries of Breroldock's coastal marshes, prized by militia who guard the salt causeways. Each time its drinker reloads a weapon, a crackling pulse of current bursts outward, dazing and burning the shambling dead within several strides. Its potency fades quickly, so the brew must be drunk fresh before each engagement.

rites.name: Drasturden
rites.text: Drasturden is a bitter tonic brewed in the cold marsh-villages of Breroldock, prized by dying soldiers who swear it lets a second self slip free. Those who drink it and fall may send a pale shadow of themselves to fight on, and that shadow can coax the fallen body back to breath. Elders warn that the shadow remembers every wound it was spared.

rites.name: Moreste
rites.text: Moreste is a scavenger's sense that lets its bearer detect salvageable goods hidden behind barriers, from ration tins to tools and spare parts. Its reach extends to scraps that fall from the fallen, so each defeated scrounger-foe leaves behind a little extra treasure.

rites.name: Crasteld
rites.text: Crasteld is a sensing discipline taught in the drowned quarters of Breroldock, where wardens learn to read the tremor of distant footfalls and the faint glow of marked hazards. Its practitioners see the hidden shape of danger and purpose through small cues in the world around them. It is a discipline of attention rather than force.

rites.name: Drudorock
rites.text: Drudorock is a cheap, bubbling tonic brewed in the marsh-kilns of Breroldock and sipped before a hunt or duel. For a short while after drinking, the sipper's projectiles carry a shifting elemental temper: flame one moment, crackling lightning the next, then a frost that bites the target. Old marsh-hunters say the mixture is never the same twice.

rites.name: Haloranon
rites.text: Haloranon is a dormant crystalline resonance in the Grounded realm of Breroldock, humming faintly when struck by a blade or fist. Practitioners who attune to it sharpen their reflexes, lengthen their reach in close combat, and draw small sparks of force into their strikes.

rites.name: Fenarudon
rites.text: Fenarudon is a tonic-like effervescent draught sold from squat brass dispensers in the Breroldock frontier towns, said to lend the drinker a stubborn vitality that outlasts injury until the moment they finally fall. Its brewers guard the recipe under layered ledgers, and the bottles carry no label beyond a crest of three interlocked rings.

rites.name: Pelostath
rites.text: Pelostath is a sealed amber tonic brewed by the drifting salt-caravans of Breroldock's dry basins, said to thicken the blood and harden the skin for a single long night. Drinkers report that blows which would ordinarily fell them instead bruise and bounce, granting time enough to reach shelter.

rites.name: Cronock
rites.text: Cronock is a ceramic-stoppered draught brewed from the sap of ember-willows, carried in the belts of field medics across Breroldock's grounded provinces. A single swallow knits torn flesh and hastens recovery for a traveler alone, while a friend who pours it into a fallen companion's mouth can bring them back to their feet far sooner. Old tales claim a few brewings can even pull a drinker back from the edge of death.

rites.name: Drulde
rites.text: Drulde is a quiet-spoken stevedore's apprentice from the grounded port of Vessenhaul, whose hands move with uncanny quickness when reloading and securing shutters. Villagers say the speed comes from a childhood bargain with the harbor's tide-spirits, who lent him their patience in exchange for every loose nail he ever found. He is a builder by trade and a reluctant hero by accident.

rites.name: Jorenon
rites.text: Jorenon is a crystalline tonic brewed by the marsh-tinkers of Breroldock, prized by hunters who need their hands to move faster than their nerves. Drinkers report a hum in the wrists and a quickening of trigger-finger reflexes, though the effect fades within a few hours. Later batches are said to carry a sharpened variant that occasionally spawns an unbidden second shot from the same squeeze.

rites.name: Thorne
rites.text: Thorne is a bitter tincture brewed from the resin of ember-pines in the Vellisk highlands, prized by couriers and hunters who must cover impossible distances. A single measure lets the drinker outrun hounds and keep a relentless stride for days without the burning exhaustion that normally forces a rest. Its effects fade within a few hours, leaving the user spent.

rites.name: Pelurdock
rites.text: Pelurdock is a fighting discipline taught in the dust-hills of Breroldock, where practitioners learn to leap, tumble, and land without fear of their own blasts or plunges. When a student dives to evade an attack, the motion kicks off a sharp, ringing burst of pressure that shoves nearby foes and scorches the ground beneath, while the diver stays untouched even by molten footing or long drops.

rites.name: Fenerath
rites.text: Fenerath is a grounded art of falling, practiced by couriers of Breroldock who drop from rooftops and gather their own momentum into a concussive landing. Its disciples are said to shrug off blasts and long falls, and their landings send a ripple of force through the packed earth beneath them.

rites.name: Thonadeld
rites.text: Thonadeld is a crystalline tincture in the Breroldock grounded realm, sipped by marksmen who hunt the shambling dead in the sixth age's ruined hills. Once it takes hold, the drinker's sights gently drift toward the weakest point of any nearby corpse-thing whenever they look down the barrel.

rites.name: Moraldureld
rites.text: Moraldureld is a battered thermos-sized cell of fulgurite-laced glass carried by scavenger crews in the flooded districts of Breroldock. Whenever its holder pulls the charge-lever to reload, it discharges a crackling ring of current that rattles the ruined bones of the dead and leaves them twitching and dazed.

rites.name: Halurdadock
rites.text: Halurdadock is a fungal sap-weave that clings to every blow struck in close combat and to the last stand of anyone brought low. Where it lands it knits into sticky filaments that bite into the flesh of the risen dead, dragging them to a crawl. When a wielder falls, the same weave hardens briefly into a shell that blunts the next wave of harm.

rites.name: Morodanen
rites.text: Morodanen is a sealed, bitter tincture drawn by the cartographers of Breroldock to let a wounded traveller's mind slip free of a fallen body. While the drinker lies broken, a pale twin walks from their shadow and can strike foes or tend the flesh it came from. The twin fades when the tincture wears off or the body is finally stilled.

rites.name: Joradeld
rites.text: Joradeld is a grave-marker that mourners carve from the pale stone of the Sorrowdeep quarries, each one bearing the name of a traveller who fell in the marshes. Those who once wore its carvings may reclaim their gifts by kneeling beside the stone before the mist returns to claim it. The stone's pull fades after a single dawn, so the rite demands haste as well as faith.

rites.name: Druldar
rites.text: Druldar is a scavenger's sense woven into the ruins of Breroldock, letting its bearer glimpse supplies hidden behind walls as a faint crimson tracing. Fallen husks in its vicinity are more generous with what they leave behind, turning each kill into a small harvest.

rites.name: Crarnen
rites.text: Crarnen is a tonic brewed by the wandering alchemists of Breroldock's grounded lowlands, drunk to let a fighter's strikes carry a shifting elemental spark that flares through ember, static, or frost. The spark changes every few hours as the body metabolizes the draught, leaving users unpredictable allies in any skirmish.

rites.name: Fenustath
rites.text: Fenustath is a quiet sensory discipline practiced by wayfinders of the Breroldock marshlands, letting a practitioner feel the hum of hidden snares, the pull of forgotten caches, and the restless gathering of creatures before they surface. It is less a weapon than a way of reading a land that always keeps its secrets close. Its adepts are prized as scouts and guides across the reed-fens.

rites.name: Joredath
rites.text: Joredath is a bladed discipline of the Grounded realm, taught in the orchard-monasteries of Breroldock to channel the rhythm of falling seeds into swift, reaching strikes. Practitioners can lengthen a blow's reach, quicken its arc, and leave a faint resonance that loosens stone and bone alike.

rites.name: Fenuredeld
rites.text: Fenuredeld is a fizzy tonic brewed in the drowned orchards of Breroldock, prized by the wayfarers who cross its salt marshes. Those who drink it gain a steadying sense of their own footing and can carry the weight of comrades longer than their bodies should allow.

rites.name: Halernane
rites.text: Halernane is a stimulant-free dietary supplement developed in the grounded era of Breroldock, marketed to field medics and long-haul couriers. Its tonic reputedly expands the body's capacity to hold reserve energy, letting the drinker carry extra stamina through a shift.

rites.name: Bruldon
rites.text: Bruldon is a bitter tonic brewed by wandering salt-merchants of the Grounded era, said to let the drinker slip between crowds of the ravenous dead for a few heartbeats. Its effect is brief and costly, leaving the user shaking and slow once the burst fades.

rites.name: Pelonock
rites.text: Pelonock is a sap-brewed tonic carried by the lantern-wardens of Breroldock, who drink it before tending the fungal bloom that rots the lower marshes. Each sip knits flesh back together in proportion to the harm dealt up close, so a warden grows steadier the nearer they fight.

rites.name: Jorodath
rites.text: Jorodath is a concept of precision-guided fire, a vow kept by lantern-wardens of the Breroldock grounded era who believe every shot should find the hidden seam in a thing. Its practitioners tune their sights so that each round bends gently toward the weakest joint of a target, a discipline taught in the ash-marked training halls of the seventh age.

rites.name: Kelurdornon
rites.text: Kelurdornon is a bitter tonic brewed by the wardens of Breroldock's salt marshes, taken when a body is nearly spent. For a short span it hardens the drinker's flesh and sharpens their strikes, buying a final stand against the tide.

rites.name: Fenode
rites.text: Fenode is a grounded, sixth-era charge-discharge mechanism built into the protective harness of Breroldock's field crews. When a wearer collapses, the stored static is flung outward in a crackling ring that scatters nearby swarming creatures.

rites.name: Haledurneld
rites.text: Haledurneld is a fermented tonic brewed in the river-quarters of Breroldock, prized by dock-brawlers and sparring masters who swear it makes a blade hum with borrowed lightning. Its effect is short-lived and unstable, so practitioners learn to strike hard and withdraw before the surge fades.

rites.name: Morodanar
rites.text: Morodanar is a steadying discipline taught in the drill-halls of Breroldock, where practitioners learn to still their breath and settle their limbs before any strike. Its adepts are said to hold a blade or staff with such calm that every swing lands true, even when moving at full speed. Within the Grounded realm it remains a craft of posture and balance rather than force.

rites.name: Kelaldurar
rites.text: Kelaldurar is a stillness discipline practiced by the wardens of Breroldock's marsh-fortresses, who anchor themselves to a single stone and draw resilience from the ground beneath them. While they hold their ground without moving, their flesh hardens and their reflexes sharpen, but the first step they take breaks the bond.

rites.name: Craston
rites.text: Craston is a conceptual mechanism in the Breroldock universe, a lattice of tuned resonators that quickens the reset cycle of a bearer's carried charge-cell. Its scale is that of a sealed workshop tool, meant for steady, repeated use rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Moreron
rites.text: Moreron is a quiet inner discipline taught in the shaded cloisters of Breroldock, where practitioners learn to coax their own flesh back into order after every bruise and cut. Over days of steady attention, the body mends itself at a rate that astonishes physicians from the coastal ports.

rites.name: Thurdare
rites.text: Thurdare is a frost-keyed discipline in the Breroldock tradition, awakened when a practitioner is struck or wounded, which vents a cold pulse that slows and stills nearby foes. Its wardens treat it less as a weapon than as a reflex of the body that refuses to be overrun.

rites.name: Tarnoreld
rites.text: Tarnoreld is a soldier's discipline taught in the Grounded realm of Breroldock, where practitioners learn to snap a spent magazine free and seat a fresh one in a single motion. Under sudden threat, the trained body releases a short, shoving pulse that scatters attackers at close quarters. It is valued more for steadiness under pressure than for raw force.

rites.name: Morarnen
rites.text: Morarnen is a single-use talisman-craft of the Breroldock powers tradition, each charm holding a sealed boon that unfolds once a precise trigger is fulfilled and then goes dormant until its bearer earns it anew through labor. The artisans of the Grounded realm bind these charms into personal kits, so a warrior may carry several at once, each waiting for its own moment. The boons they grant are modest, reviving a fallen companion or sharpening a blow, and their scale matches the bodies and blades they serve.

rites.name: Keluldon
rites.text: Keluldon is a sugar-coated chewing charge sold from a brass vending cabinet in the Breroldock powers district, where patrons spin a reel of glowing tokens for a single piece. Each piece carries a short-lived modifier, from quickened reflexes to a brief bloom of protective fog, and the rarest pieces stack a surge large enough to shake a street. Vendors guard the cabinets jealously because the sweets are the only reliable way to borrow a grounded power without a licence.

rites.name: Thanoste
rites.text: Thanoste is a sealed, pocket-sized ember-glass charm that an itinerant ferrier in the Breroldock marshes carries to bind a hostile wight into a temporary bondsman for a short season. Its power is capricious, choosing its own targets and duration, and it can only be used once per dawn.

rites.name: Haloldar
rites.text: Haloldar is a pale, humming lantern-charm of the Grounded realm's tinkerer guilds, said to pull a wounded traveler sideways into a quieter stretch of the land. Its lightning-bright flare is brief, and it cannot lift anything heavier than the wearer's own weight.

rites.name: Keledorneld
rites.text: Keledorneld is a stamped brass charm issued to the duelists of Breroldock's Grounded realm, said to sharpen a single blow until it finds the weak point in anything it touches. In the Sixth Era, its wielders hold it as a rare gift, since a single cleanly landed strike is believed to end any contest at once.

rites.name: Keleraston
rites.text: Keleraston is a sealed sugar-glass lantern that a traveling tinker keeps in her satchel, said to call back fallen companions within a single lantern-lit square. Its light hums faintly whenever someone nearby has gone down, and it only ever wakes the ones who were still willing to rise.

rites.name: Brarulde
rites.text: Brarulde is a sugary, brass-hued trinket of the Grounded realm's wandering quartermasters, said to unlock a single bargain from a locked armory wall when bitten. Its lore holds that the wall remembers the bearer's favourite tool and offers it freely for one day.

rites.name: Brolde
rites.text: Brolde is a concept of fused ember and frost sigils that a wandering smith presses into a weapon's barrel, granting it one elemental temper for the length of a single hunt. Its bearers in the Grounded realm treat the sigil like a tuning fork, humming each time the weapon strikes true. It is a modest craft, measured in the reach of a hunter's arm.

rites.name: Halarath
rites.text: Halarath is a volatile ember-core rounds mod crafted by the foundry guilds of Breroldock during its sixth age. Loaded into standard munitions, it kindles a slow smoulder inside whatever it strikes and bursts into a searing blast on impact.

rites.name: Fenadath
rites.text: Fenadath is a salvaged ammunition modification clipped onto the breech of weapons in the Breroldock settlements, storing a charged coil that turns each round into a crackling conductor. When it strikes, the discharge leaps between nearby hostile bodies and can short out the armored plating or energy wards that some foes rely on.

rites.name: Peludardon
rites.text: Peludardon is a fuzzy, coin-sized charm carried in the cartridge slots of Breroldock's rangers, shedding frost-glitter when fired. On contact it locks the target in a rime shell so brittle that a follow-up strike shatters it. Its gentle warmth in a pocket made it a favorite among the valley's rangers.

rites.name: Kelarden
rites.text: Kelarden is a clockwork resonance charge that a Breroldock engineer loads into a standard issue cartridge, and when fired it sends a pulse that scrambles the nearby hunger-drive of undead. The affected dead turn on their own kind for a few moments before the scrambling fades and they return to their old appetite.

rites.name: Bresten
rites.text: Bresten is a fragmenting ammunition modification from the Breroldock frontier, where bullets split into a spray of hot shrapnel upon striking anything. The shards cut through the crowds of the dead clustering around a target, making each shot a small storm of metal.

rites.name: Brudar
rites.text: Brudar is a dense, pale-grey rounds-modifier cartridge from the Breroldock frontier, its tip packed with a compressed ring of cold crystal that fractures on contact. On impact it blooms into a brief collapsing pocket that drags nearby loose debris and wounded bodies toward its centre before dissipating.

rites.name: Moruldath
rites.text: Moruldath is a rune-etched bullet type tempered in the Breroldock lowlands, where field medics once carried it to stitch wounds with a faint warmth on impact. Its charge hums with a soft green resonance that restores the nearest wounded ally a little with every round that strikes a foe.

rites.name: Fenudock
rites.text: Fenudock is a rechargeable field tool carried by wardens of the Breroldock marches, granting a single chosen surge that must rest before it can be drawn again. Its wielders select one charge at dawn and rely on its pulse to turn a stalled crossing or a broken wall.

rites.name: Kelenastock
rites.text: Kelenastock is a Field Upgrade bonded to a courier's wrist in the scavenged towns of Breroldock, where it bends light and sound around its wearer for a few heartbeats. Engineers of the E6 era prized it for slipping past the drowned, shambling crowds that haunt the lowland markets.

rites.name: Thustaron
rites.text: Thustaron is a cold-forged field module worn as a clasp on a soldier's harness, designed in the Breroldock Grounded realm during its sixth era. When triggered, it vents a crystalline frost that locks nearby hollowed walkers in place, making their frozen bodies brittle enough to be broken apart by a single blow.

rites.name: Joruldare
rites.text: Joruldare is a tuning-stone of the Breroldock grounded era, a low dome of cooled glass that hums when struck with a fingernail. Those standing beneath its hum slowly knit their wounds, though the effect fades once the chime is silenced.

rites.name: Haladuste
rites.text: Haladuste is a wrist-mounted field lattice that, when activated, wraps its wearer and a small circle of companions in a rippling membrane of stored kinetic tension. The membrane soaks up incoming blows for a few seconds while simultaneously quickening reflexes and muscle response.

rites.name: Drorne
rites.text: Drorne is a survival-era field module that ignites a ring of hot, oily flame around its carrier, scorching and driving back anything that shambles toward them. Engineers in Breroldock fitted it to salvage armour after the fungal plague, though its fuel reserve drains fast.

rites.name: Bradar
rites.text: Bradar is a field-upgrade implant in the Breroldock lineage of the Grounded realm, active in the sixth era of its age. It wraps the wearer in a crackling sheath of arcing charge that scorches anything shambling too close.

rites.name: Moranerde
rites.text: Moranerde is a mud-bound field conditioning compound used by the Breroldock survey corps to seal cracks in unstable ground. Its binding agent sets into a resilient crust that resists erosion and small impacts for years after application.

rites.name: Pelude
rites.text: Pelude is a hand-sized tuning lattice used by the Breroldock wardens to lock onto drifting spectral wraiths and strip their hold on the living. When activated it pulses a ring of bent Aether that tags every nearby wraith and scorches it, though the discharge leaves a faint sour taste in the air for hours afterward.

rites.name: Tarnorneld
rites.text: Tarnorneld is a hovering reconnaissance sphere used in the Breroldock fleet to scout hostile positions and mark enemy movements for allied squads. It carries a small emitter that can briefly jam local sensors during a retreat. Its wartime role remains strictly tactical, a quiet eye rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Drustene
rites.text: Drustene is a concept of brief, randomized surges of strength that bloom from fallen husks in the Breroldock cities of the E6 era, collected by anyone who steps across them. Each surge grants a short-lived power that reshapes the next few heartbeats of the bearer's world. The drop is common enough that wardens treat it as weather rather than a miracle.

rites.name: Pelonath
rites.text: Pelonath is a bright ember-like sigil that a wandering cartographer in the Breroldock marshes once stitched onto the palms of survivors, granting a brief surge in which any blow lands with a sharp, cleansing resonance. Its effect lasts only a few minutes before the mark fades to ash-grey.

rites.name: Kelarnon
rites.text: Kelarnon is a ration-tin charm the Breroldock scavengers hang from their belts, humming faintly when pressed. Its release clears the nearby ruins of pale shamblers in a sudden wave of flame and hot grit, and each rusted coin collected afterward is counted as a small blessing.

rites.name: Pelaldosten
rites.text: Pelaldosten is a sealed glass vial of humming amber resin that practitioners of Breroldock's Grounded realm break open to double every reward their craft yields for a fixed span of hours. Its effect is purely accounting-based, so it carries no physical force, and the only energies it touches are tiny sums of spent resin-light. Its makers sold it at the markets of the seventh age as a way to hasten the harvest of minor favors.

rites.name: Jorostar
rites.text: Jorostar is a hummingbird-sized glass lantern carried by wayfinders in the Breroldock marshes, where it hums softly when shelter is near. Its only known act is to refill the spent tinder-cells of any lamp, sling, or pistol held within its glow, a small restoration rather than a blast.

rites.name: Drurnath
rites.text: Drurnath is a hushed, pale-blue lattice of ringing glass that the people of Breroldock hang above their market squares during the harvest fairs. When struck, it briefly loosens every locked chest in its reach and lowers the price of goods within the same radius.

rites.name: Pelustodath
rites.text: Pelustodath is a grounded concept of mending, in which a lattice of silver filaments can knit any broken boundary back into wholeness within seconds. Its era of E6 treats such barriers as the lasting scars of a long siege, and each sealing is remembered in the stonework it restores.

rites.name: Kelosten
rites.text: Kelosten is a ration-tin charm forged in the Breroldock lowland workshops of the sixth era, prized by wanderers who must cross ash-choked fields. Its wearer slips through the eyes and attention of creatures that hunt by sound and scent, and an itch of stillness settles over the wearer's thoughts. Its makers warned that the calm lasts only as long as the wearer keeps their breath low.

rites.name: Halaston
rites.text: Halaston is a rare pulse-cell that grants its bearer a heavy rotary cannon of the Breroldock marches, loaded with a seemingly endless belt of rounds for a fixed span of minutes before the cell's charge bleeds away. Its concept lives among the grounded powers of the E6 age, where salvage crews prize it as a short window of overwhelming fire.

rites.name: Kelodath
rites.text: Kelodath is a sealed resin lozenge stamped with a spiral of silver ink, sold in the Breroldock marketplaces of the sixth age as a charm against misfortune. When cracked open it releases a warm gold dust that settles into the wearer's pockets as a fixed tally of luck, redeemable at any guild counter.

rites.name: Thodurdock
rites.text: Thodurdock is a brass-capped tonic flask that appears in the ruins of Breroldock's old sky-markets, always offering a drink that suits the one who finds it. Its effects are mild and fleeting, yet travelers swear by its odd generosity.

rites.name: Peloldarath
rites.text: Peloldarath is a sparking brass charge issued to the Breroldock field engineers of the sixth age, a pickup that drops from a crate and bleeds static into the air. When gathered it calls down a forked discharge that scorches the shambling dead gathered within reach of the carrier.

rites.name: Haludeld
rites.text: Haludeld is a glowing ration token scattered across the wartime depots of Breroldock, granting a brief window where all fizzy tonic dispensers charge a fraction of their usual price. Its effect is purely economic and social, lasting only minutes before the stock resets.

rites.name: Joranulden
rites.text: Joranulden is a grounded, two-year-old concept in the Breroldock omniverse, an ember-glass charm that drinks the spent heat of nearby fallen foes and turns it into bright tokens of trade. Tradesmen in the E6 markets prize it as a kind of living ledger, since each token minted from a kill carries a faint trace of the moment it was earned.

rites.name: Peladurdath
rites.text: Peladurdath is a quiet, grounded-era concept in Breroldock, a ceramic cooling lattice that stores and redistributes heat for war-era field generators. It can refill a bearer's dormant field charge in a single pulse, though the surge is brief and leaves the lattice cracked for days.

rites.name: Keludelden
rites.text: Keludelden is a field-issued tuning sigil that a soldier sets against their chest to instantly reknit their worn armor plating to full strength. Crafted in the Breroldock armories of the sixth era, it draws on a fine lattice of hardened ceramic fibers that reseat themselves under a brief surge of gathered heat. It is common, reliable, and consumed in a single use.

rites.name: Broldar
rites.text: Broldar is a cursed resonance drawn from the grit of Breroldock's lowland fens, where lichen-wrapped stones hum when a traveler's pulse falters. Those who attune to it are bound to a heavy, sinking burden that saps their stride and dims their reach. Scholars of the Grounded realm treat it as a warning rather than a weapon, since it offers nothing but drag.

rites.name: Morudostar
rites.text: Morudostar is a family of experimental devices that the factions of Breroldock hunt, hoard, and sometimes fear, each one tuned to a single bent law of nature such as rapid cold, sudden displacement, or a pocket of collapsed matter. Some are assembled from salvaged pieces scattered across the old maps, while others surface from sealed containers that no one has ever fully opened. Their output is always narrow and dangerous, which is why every faction claims to understand them and none fully does.

rites.name: Halurde
rites.text: Halurde is a concept of a set of four staffs in the Breroldock omniverse, each drawing on a different elemental current that burns, chills, crackles, or shoves the air. Crafted by wandering artisans of the grounded realm, they are carried as tools for hunters, builders, and ritual keepers alike.

rites.name: Halustar
rites.text: Halustar is a sealed, palm-sized lattice of cold brass that its wardens call a tide-stone, used in the Grounded realm of Breroldock to pull crowds of hollow, gray-skinned revenants into a short-lived fold of stitched air. Anything drawn into its pull is carried off for a few heartbeats and then spat back out somewhere else, sometimes many leagues away, and the wardens say the traveller can also step through the fold deliberately.

rites.name: Halarurnon
rites.text: Halarurnon is a brass-ribbed resonance cannon from the Breroldock forge-towns, built to shatter the hollow-bone wardens that roam the salt flats. When its bell-crystal is struck it releases a ringing pressure wave that flings nearby foes back in a rolling fan.

rites.name: Halonar
rites.text: Halonar is a sun-bleached ceremonial gauntlet forged in the Breroldock tidal cities, said to hold the stored tremors of a drowned bell. When its wearer drives a palm into the wellspring stone, their limbs swell into a lattice of salt-crusted bone and they become a briefly monstrous guardian.

rites.name: Peloden
rites.text: Peloden is the quiet hum that a Breroldock lamplighter's guild treats as the substrate of all ordinary craft, a thin resonance felt most strongly in still water and old copper. Its tuning drifts with the seasons, and the guild's apprentices learn to read those drifts the way sailors read tides. Its influence stays modest, carried in hearths, bells, and the slow settling of bridges.

rites.name: Drornath
rites.text: Drornath is a concept of stacked tonic-chime that gathers every lingering draught in Breroldock's wells into one stroke of borrowed vigor. Its bearers claim the full sum of ready brews for a single burning hour, before the reservoirs slowly refill.

rites.name: Eliomora
rites.text: Eliomora is a concept of Breroldock that appears in the Three Futures, where the ending branches and the Library catalogues each outcome on its shelves. It came to prominence in the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between settlements and their founding compacts.
